title: Deliver experimental witnessed-access Jury 0.x portable vault
description:
## Outcome

Deliver an experimental witnessed-access Jury 0.x portable encrypted vault. Governed items require fresh signed approval and distinct witness contributions for the exact revision seal and action manifest before read, inject, or exec crosses the guarded item boundary.

Direct slots remain an explicit unilateral bootstrap, recovery, or low-assurance mode. Any usable direct slot suppresses the quorum claim for that item.

## Release Boundary

The active release has 29 outcomes: J01A, J01B, J02-J14, J16-J26, plus J19A-J19C. J15 compatibility and J19R/J19D/J19E external-review work are standalone deferred tasks excluded from active readiness and estimates.

J01A/J01B gate shared and direct cryptographic primitives. J19A-J19C freeze the witnessed construction corpus; J19 binds its exact artifacts and provider inputs after a fresh solo verification pass. After J25, J26 reruns the release checks from a clean checkout or equivalent clean worktree and binds the exact source, verifier, provider lock data, build inputs, and artifacts.

This is a one-person project with zero external-review budget. Models, coding agents, alternate implementations, tests, self-review, and clean builds are engineering evidence, never independent security review. Every 0.x release remains externally unreviewed pre-alpha software unsuitable for real secrets.

title: J01A — Freeze core cryptographic requirements and the v1 suite
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Freeze the shared primitive suite and direct-slot construction used by the experimental witnessed-first release. J19 owns the additional distributed construction and exact-artifact gate. This work does not establish that Jury is safe for real secrets. No production provider adapter or cryptographic implementation may land in J01A.

## Why This Task Exists

Provider availability must not choose Jury's security properties by accident.
Freezing the required properties, nonclaims, alternatives, contexts, and failure
behavior first gives J01B and J19 one stable provider-neutral contract to prove.

## Outcome

`docs/security/jury-v1-suite.md` contains a reviewable property matrix,
alternative comparison, explicit post-quantum and compliance decisions, and one
exact provider-neutral primitive suite and direct-slot construction before any
provider is selected.

## Required Work

- define required classical confidentiality/authenticity, recipient-compromise
  history exposure, nonce-misuse, key-binding/commitment, and failure behavior;
- decide whether stored recipient slots must resist harvest-now/decrypt-later
  attacks and separately whether signatures need post-quantum authenticity;
- compare classical RFC 9180 HPKE, pure ML-KEM HPKE, and
  X25519+ML-KEM-768 hybrid HPKE using exact key/ciphertext sizes, performance,
  portability, provider maturity, vector quality, and draft churn;
- compare AES-256-GCM-SIV, one-key/one-seal RFC 8439
  ChaCha20-Poly1305, and the exact expired XChaCha Internet-Draft profile for
  storage; do not equate larger nonces with misuse resistance;
- compare strict Ed25519 with a reviewed hybrid-signature alternative if PQ
  authenticity is required;
- freeze exact KEM/HPKE mode, AEADs, KDFs and contexts, hash/signature rules,
  Argon2id profiles, device-factor combiner, randomness treatment, encodings,
  limits, and error behavior;
- state that FIPS-validated deployment is a V1 non-goal and never infer a FIPS
  deployment claim from use of FIPS 203 ML-KEM;
- require one authenticated suite at lineage genesis, no negotiation or
  fallback, and authenticated re-encryption into a new lineage for migration;
- specify revision-scoped direct capsules plus descriptor/body secrets with
  fresh random `RevisionSealId` values; J19 owns the witnessed construction and
  may not weaken these suite, context, downgrade, or key-lifetime requirements.

- freeze the secret inputs, required constant-time behavior, provider/platform caveats, and local or remote observation model for every secret-bearing operation, including KEM decapsulation and implicit rejection, AEAD authentication comparisons, signature generation, KDF handling, and wrapper control flow or memory access.

## Required Verification

- independently recompute every size and security-property table entry from
  pinned primary specifications;
- demonstrate that every claimed property follows from the complete suite and
  that one weaker slot or fallback defeats the claim;
- specify positive, negative, fault, migration, and cross-provider vectors that
  J01B, J19, and J25 must realize;
- review nonce/key reuse, malformed-key/ciphertext, entropy failure, KDF
  exhaustion, draft-version substitution, secret-dependent control flow, and
  timing/validity-oracle cases at the construction level.

## Acceptance Criteria

- the matrix has no “broadly sound” or unstated property cells: each is yes, no,
  conditional with assumptions, or not required with rationale;
- HNDL resistance and PQ authenticity are explicit independent decisions;
- one exact suite and all constructions, contexts, encodings, and limits are
  frozen or J01A remains open;
- every secret-bearing operation has an explicit constant-time/side-channel
  requirement or a bounded nonclaim with an attacker-observation rationale;
- every RFC, FIPS, or draft dependency is named with exact status and revision;
- FIPS-validated deployment is explicitly out of scope;
- no algorithm negotiation, fallback, mixed active suites, or in-place suite
  mutation is permitted;
- no production provider dependency, adapter, or cryptographic implementation
  lands.
- a verifier other than the artifact author cites the exact revision and reruns
  the primary-source/size calculations before closure; a solo rerun is recorded
  honestly and does not count as independent verification.

## Dependencies

none.

## Unblocks

J01B, J05.

## Live Tracker Dependencies

None.

Unblocks J01B: `jury-qv4.1.2`.

title: J01B — Select and prove the cryptographic provider set
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Prove the shared providers and direct construction used as inputs to J19. Provider evidence and automated conformance feed but do not replace J19 exact-artifact verification and binding and do not make Jury suitable for real secrets.

## Why This Task Exists

Algorithm names do not establish provider behavior. Pinning actual implementations, feature surfaces, vectors, and wrapper normalization before product code lands prevents silent fallback, accidental dependency expansion, and security claims that exceed reproducible evidence.

## Outcome

Select the smallest provider set that implements exactly the J01A shared primitive suite and direct construction and record reproducible wrapper, supply-chain, and conformance evidence.

## Required Work

- Pin source revisions, checksums, features, MSRV, licenses, unsafe-code posture, maintenance status, and advisories.
- Document fallible entropy, allocation, malformed-input, error, and zeroization behavior without inferring guarantees.
- Map every J01A side-channel requirement to provider source evidence: constant-time guarantees, implicit rejection, comparison APIs, secret-dependent branches or memory access, and compiler/target/hardware caveats.
- Keep raw providers behind thin typed wrappers and exclude unrelated features.
- Where measurement is meaningful, add targeted differential/statistical timing tests for decapsulation, authentication, comparison, and wrapper paths; never present a passing timing test as proof of constant-time behavior.
- Bind the accepted suite, provider revisions, and vector hashes in docs/security/jury-v0-direct-crypto-gate.toml. This is a drift-prevention manifest, not a security certificate.

## Required Tests

Run provider suites at pinned revisions; compare at least two independent implementations where viable; test positive and negative semantics, canonical encodings, limits, entropy failures, zeroization paths, unsupported suites, and fallback rejection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- every provider and wrapper claim has reproducible dated evidence;
- every J01A side-channel requirement maps to provider source evidence and a
  wrapper invariant; an unknown or violated requirement keeps J01B open;
- selected providers implement exactly one J01A direct suite with no runtime fallback;
- independent implementations agree on accepted outputs and rejection semantics, or differences are normalized and tested;
- the dependency tree excludes unrelated plugin, SSH, PEM, legacy, and hazmat surfaces;
- the minimal direct-crypto gate binds the exact suite, provider revisions, specifications, and vectors;
- no provider dependency, adapter, or cryptographic implementation lands before the J01A/J01B direct gate is accepted, and no witnessed implementation lands before J19's additional exact-artifact gate;
- no certification or independent-review claim is made;
- J19 consumes the exact pinned provider behavior and vectors; no witnessed implementation may treat this direct gate as a substitute for J19 verification and binding.

## Dependencies

J01A. Unblocks J04 and J19A.

title: J02 — Extract protected bytes, redaction, and hardened filesystem primitives
J11 — Implement authorized atomic policy and item mutations
description:
## Why This Task Exists

Policy, slots, item revisions, audit, and checkpoints form one authorization transition even though they cross storage boundaries. Complete preflight plus single-primary publication prevents partial revocation, implicit downgrade, stale Git overwrite, and unsafe retry after a committed mutation.

## Outcome

Authorize, preflight, sign, audit, and atomically publish item, direct-access, witnessed-governance, and identity-lifecycle mutations with commit-compatible dry-run previews.

## Required Design Contract

- Mutations cover fields, items, batches, direct grants/revokes, owners, vault principals, approver and witness membership, same-role replacement/rotation, access mode, approval quorum, witness quorum, operation/lifetime/workload requirements, and privacy-cover reseal.
- A transition to witnessed-only proves that no usable direct slot remains and that current eligible membership can satisfy configured quorums.
- Adding any direct slot or lowering witnessed requirements is an explicit downgrade that suppresses the item quorum claim, invalidates incompatible pending requests, and requires an authenticated acknowledgement in the calling layer.
- Membership, quorum, mode, and role changes bind one policy result to all required slot/capsule, item-revision, request-invalidation, audit, and checkpoint changes.
- Determine every touched item and authorization prerequisite before decryption. Preflight rotations, signatures, bounds, capacity, and optimistic revision checks.
- Dry-run writes no shared or local bytes. Commit rechecks the preview revision under the cross-worktree lock.
- Publish one encrypted shared artifact, then advance local audit/checkpoint. Post-publication local-state failure reports committed primary success and never retries the shared mutation.
- Jury never invokes Git or stages, commits, pushes, or rewrites history.

## Required Tests

Cover every failure boundary; stale preview and checkout/reset/linked-worktree races; multi-item all-or-nothing behavior; direct, owner, approver, and witness matrices; quorum and mode transitions; direct downgrade acknowledgement and claim suppression; pending-request invalidation; rotation/replacement; cover invariance/capacity; publication/fsync faults; and secret-free results/errors.

## Dependencies

J07 and J10. Unblocks J13, J18, and J25.

## Legacy Baseline and Provenance

Use https://github.com/bpcakes/jig-sh.git at exact commit eed70cee337b0067ed92deb9fa05017b0b284605; a sibling ../jig-sh is only an object source after the commit and every selected path verifies. If the exact object or a named path is unavailable, this task blocks rather than substituting another revision, build output, or the preserved source-plan snapshot.

Inspect:

- crates/jig-vault/src/vault_tests/management.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/vault_tests/mutations.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/vault_tests/import.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/vault_tests/lifecycle.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/store.rs;
- crates/jig-vault/src/store/existing.rs.

Port collision, no-op, stale-precondition, audit-before-save, atomic-batch, redaction-downgrade, reserved-output, and publication-failure cases. Replace Vault, OpenVault, the vault-wide envelope, and v2 mutation methods.

title: J15 — Deliver post-0.x read-only Jig compatibility and copy-on-write migration
description:
## Post-0.x Compatibility Scope

This task is explicitly deferred and out of scope for the witnessed-access 0.x release. It has no parent-child relationship to the active release epic, is excluded from active readiness and estimates, and does not block J17, J25, J26, or any active release outcome. An operator may reactivate it only after J26 under a separately approved post-0.x compatibility scope.

## Why This Task Exists

Legacy migration can corrupt the only source copy or reproduce the security boundary Jury is replacing. A read-only, copy-on-write import into a fresh lineage makes every attempt reversible and independently verifiable while leaving retained legacy exposure explicit.

## Outcome

Valid legacy Jig v1/v2 vaults can be read through isolated compatibility types and copied into an absent Jury home without mutating or dual-writing the source.

## Required Work

- Accept bounded legacy inputs only through isolated read-only compatibility types; never write a legacy format.
- Require explicit source and absent, non-aliased destination.
- Create fresh Jury identifiers, keys, genesis, audit, checkpoint, and migration attestation.
- Verify legacy audit and bind the preserved archive digest.
- Prove source artifact and audit hashes remain unchanged across success and every injected failure.
- Keep identities and local rollback state outside repository destinations.
- Perform no implicit Git operation and retain explicit warnings about old full-access copies.

## Dependencies

J03, J05, J06, J07, J09, and J10. This task has no active 0.x dependents.

## Legacy Baseline and Provenance

Use https://github.com/bpcakes/jig-sh.git at exact commit eed70cee337b0067ed92deb9fa05017b0b284605; a sibling ../jig-sh is only an object source after the commit and every selected path verifies. title: J16 — Implement transfer, inspection, and ancestry merge
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

This task supplies a shared capability for the witnessed-first 0.x release. J19-J23 own protocol-specific integration; this task must preserve their guarded boundaries and the pre-alpha/no-real-secrets warning.

## Project Boundary

Jury is a standalone witnessed-first CLI/TUI plus self-hostable witness service using jury-vault format v1. It must not depend on Jig at runtime, expose private keys or plaintext through adapters, or use non-generic fixtures. It is not independently reviewed and must not be used for real secrets.

## Why This Task Exists

Transfer distributes portable ciphertext, not recovery authority. Signed envelopes, ancestry validation, and typed fork rejection permit safe offline exchange without including identities or pretending local export proves delivery.

## Required Design Contract

- Transfer contains the complete shared ciphertext artifact plus signed envelope metadata, never identities, local audit/checkpoint, or local receipts.
- Inspect is public/opaque by default and projects only names decryptable by an explicitly selected identity.
- Import requires exact genesis and policy/item ancestry; permit strict descendant and independent-item merge, reject policy or same-item forks, removed writers, old epochs, rollback, and cross-lineage rollover merge.
- First install uses explicit genesis-fingerprint trust. Export status is local evidence only and never claims delivery.

## Outcome

Portable encrypted shared state can be exported, inspected, imported, and
merged when ancestry permits without carrying local identities or audit.

## Scope

- implement bounded transfer envelope and digest;
- implement public inspection and optional accessible-name projection;
- enforce genesis, policy, item-proof, and checkpoint relationships;
- permit strict descendants and independent-item merges only when signatures
  and ancestry prove safety;
- reject same-item forks without explicit recovery;
- record local export status without claiming delivery.

## Required Tests

- truncation, replacement, wrong genesis, rollback, and forks;
- independent-item merge and same-item conflict;
- inaccessible-name non-disclosure;
- no identity/audit/checkpoint/local receipt in transfer;
- atomic import and dry-run.

## Acceptance Criteria

- raw copy and transfer semantics are documented honestly;
- import cannot silently discard a valid local branch;
- export status never claims recipient delivery.
- ordinary textual Git merge cannot produce an accepted Jury artifact;
- semantic diff is value-free by default and inaccessible names remain hidden;
- three-way merge cannot discard a valid local branch or accept Git identity as Jury authority;
- old and divergent checkouts never lower retained local ancestry.
- merge never silently selects a direct downgrade, lower quorum, revived witness/approver, or stale quorum claim;

## Plan Dependencies

J05, J06, J07, J09, J10.

## Unblocks

J18, J24, J25.

## Live Tracker Dependencies

- J05: `jury-qv4.2.4`
- J06: `jury-qv4.2.5`
- J07: `jury-qv4.2.6`
- J09: `jury-qv4.2.8`
- J10: `jury-qv4.2.9`

## Legacy Baseline and Provenance

No Jig v2 code is an architectural baseline for this task. Reuse only generic primitives already owned by another Jury dependency; witnessed integration is owned by J19-J23.

The reviewed Jig source is `https://github.com/bpcakes/jig-sh.git` at commit `eed70cee337b0067ed92deb9fa05017b0b284605`; a verified sibling `../jig-sh` may supply the object database. Preserve whole-file history where the task explicitly approves extraction. Otherwise port behavior and negative tests with source-path annotations. Never add a Jury runtime dependency on Jig or reuse v2 security oracles that assume one passphrase, one DEK, whole-vault unlock, public item names, or in-place migration.

## Jig v3 Retirement Provenance

This task carries the Jury disposition for B14. The exact unshipped source design remains in `docs/provenance/jig-vault-security-scopes-plan.source.md`; implementation follows this Bead's Jury-native contract.


## Git-backed Diff and Merge Amendment

Treat Git as an untrusted carrier for the J16 artifact. Add bounded public verification, value-free semantic diff over two explicit artifacts, and ancestry-aware three-way merge over explicit base/ours/theirs inputs. Every input is independently parsed and authenticated. Merge accepts strict descendants and valid independent-item progress only; it rejects wrong genesis, rollback, removed writers, old epochs, policy forks, same-item forks, cross-lineage state, conflict markers, and partial driver output.

The operations require no identity by default and reveal only public opaque metadata; an explicitly selected identity may project only names it can decrypt from fully validated state. They may back an opt-in Git diff/merge driver, but missing or failed integration leaves a conflict and never falls back to textual merge. Git authorship, commit signatures, PR approval, and Git's chosen merge base grant no Jury authority. Compare checkouts with J09 retained state before private use.

## Witnessed Policy and Downgrade Merge Requirements

- Authenticate and merge witnessed membership, quorum, access-mode, workload, pending-request invalidation, and direct-slot claim-suppression state under the same ancestry rules as other public policy.
- Reject independent branches that change the same witnessed policy scope, introduce a usable direct slot, lower a quorum, or revive a revoked approver/witness; never choose the weaker branch automatically.
- Require the merged artifact to recompute mode and quorum-claim status from validated slots and policy rather than trusting cached labels.

## Additional Required Tests

Cover direct-versus-witnessed policy forks, concurrent membership/quorum edits, direct-slot introduction on either branch, revoked actor resurrection, pending-request invalidation, and stale cached quorum claims.

title: J17 — Deliver owner backup, restore, and recovery drills
J18 — Implement capacity preflight and authenticated rollover
description:
## Why This Task Exists

Bounded append-only histories eventually reach hard limits, but pruning would erase evidence and mutate the lineage being verified. Authenticated rollover to a fresh lineage is the only capacity escape that preserves the old artifact, requires new trust, and keeps retained-copy limitations honest.

## Outcome

Every mutation predicts hard limits, and owners can create a fresh Jury-v1 lineage with a signed source bridge, fresh witnessed topology, and anchored initial checkpoint before history caps are exhausted or the authenticated suite changes.

## Required Work

- Compute count and encoded-size results before mutation and report stable safe headroom with typed capacity errors.
- Implement owner-only dry-run and absent-home rollover.
- Generate new vault/item identifiers, revision secrets/seal identifiers, direct slots or witnessed capsules, ciphertext, and revision-one chains without reusing old contributions or authorization transcripts.
- Bind a canonical bootstrap manifest into the source bridge.
- For governed items, bind the new lineage policy, approver membership, witness membership, quorums, suite, and revision-one seals; register fresh witness topology and establish the initial replay checkpoint/external anchor through J23 operations before declaring the lineage witnessed-ready.
- Treat missing, stale, restored, or partially rotated witnesses as not ready; never fall back to direct access.
- Reuse absent-home rollover for suite migration: authenticate the source suite, re-encrypt every active item under one supported destination suite, bind old/new genesis IDs, source terminal revision, and item digests, and never mix suites in one lineage.
- Emit a value-free adoption manifest for a later explicit tracked-artifact replacement; Jury never invokes Git.
- Require new external genesis trust, backup, witness recovery drill, and redistribution.

## Required Tests

Cover every capacity boundary; rollover at cap; bridge/manifest mutation; old contribution and transcript reuse; incomplete topology registration; checkpoint/anchor split writes; restored/rotated witnesses; impossible quorum; direct fallback attempts; suite downgrade/mixing/partial re-encryption; destination path attacks; publication faults; and old-lineage preservation.

## Dependencies

J11, J16, J17, and J23. Unblocks J24, J25, and J26.

title: J03 — Implement native domain identifiers and the external adapter seam

title: J04 — Deliver encrypted vault, approver, and witness identities
description:
## Why This Task Exists

The witnessed trust model collapses if one private-key container can silently act in several roles. Separately encrypted identities and typed private operations keep vault-principal, approver, and witness authority distinct and keep every private authority outside portable vault artifacts.

## Outcome

Deliver separately purposed, encrypted vault-principal, approver, and witness identities outside portable vault artifacts. Public APIs expose typed private operations, never private key bytes.

## Required Work

- Implement bounded identity format v1 using the accepted J01A/J01B provider suite and, for contribution keys, the exact J19-bound construction.
- Define distinct VaultPrincipalIdentity, ApproverIdentity, and WitnessIdentity descriptors with role, suite, provider, public material, key identifier, and usage constraints.
- Generate independent recipient, signing, and contribution material; validate public/private correspondence and prohibit silent derivation, reuse, or cross-role substitution.
- Expose typed operations for item unwrap, exact-manifest approval signing, decision/receipt/checkpoint signing, and one revision-bound witness contribution as applicable to each role.
- Validate Argon2id parameters before allocation and preserve exact passphrase bytes.
- Support named and explicit-file selection, passphrase resealing, role-preserving key rotation/replacement, and disjoint identity/vault homes.
- Keep device protectors behind IdentityProtector; advertise only providers that pass conformance and never silently substitute a fallback.
- Keep witness replay/checkpoint recovery operations in J23; this task owns key custody and role-specific identity transitions.

## Required Tests

Cover wrong credentials, corrupt headers, hostile KDF parameters, selector/path attacks, entropy/provider failures, cancellation, passphrase boundaries, cross-role substitution, contribution-key misuse, rotation/replacement, protected-memory exits, and secret-free logs/errors.

## Dependencies

J01B, J02, and J19. Unblocks J07, J08, J09, J17, and J20.

title: J05 — Freeze the bounded direct/witnessed Jury vault format
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Freeze format v1 with final direct and witnessed slot fields before implementation. There is no shipped direct-only predecessor and no later witnessed-format amendment.

## Why This Task Exists

Signatures, cross-implementation vectors, parser bounds, and safe Git transport all depend on one byte-exact public format. Freezing direct and witnessed fields together prevents a later schema amendment from introducing downgrade, negotiation, or incompatible preimages after implementation begins.

## Outcome

VaultFileV1 has bounded parse types, exact canonical preimages, deterministic portable JSON, and independently generated positive and negative vectors for both access paths.

## Required Work

- Define header, genesis, journals, envelopes, direct slots, witnessed slots, revisions, tombstones, rollover, and migration attestations.
- Bind every descriptor/body seal and capsule to a fresh RevisionSealId, content role, revision, policy, suite, vault, item, and epoch.
- Encode exactly one authenticated suite per lineage with no negotiation, fallback, mixed active suites, or in-place suite mutation.
- Include no epoch root or reusable witness contribution field.
- Sign typed binary preimages while JSON remains bounded presentation storage.
- Keep identity, checkpoint, local audit receipts, witness replay/checkpoint databases, locks, recovery state, and local paths outside .jury/vault.json.
- Reject duplicate keys and identifiers, alternate encodings, unknown versions, oversized input, conflict markers, and truncated merge output before private work.

## Required Tests

title: J06 — Implement signed policy replay and exact access evaluation
description:
## Why This Task Exists

Authorization must come from one replayable signed history rather than current configuration, private catalog contents, or caller interpretation. A deterministic normalized state makes ownership, direct access, both witnessed quorums, and every downgrade independently auditable and deny-by-default.

## Outcome

Replay public signed policy from genesis into one deterministic normalized state that governs direct authority and witnessed membership, approval, quorum, workload, and downgrade rules without decrypting private item names.

## Required Design Contract

- Model vault principals, approvers, and witnesses as distinct subject classes. Only human vault principals may own; at least one human owner always remains.
- Model direct reader/writer roles separately from approver eligibility and witness membership.
- For every governed item, bind access mode, eligible approvers, eligible witnesses, approval quorum, witness quorum, allowed operations, maximum request lifetime, and workload constraints.
- Quorums count distinct active identities, are bounded by membership, and deny on unknown, duplicated, revoked, or cross-role subjects.
- Any usable direct slot makes access unilateral for that item and suppresses the witnessed/quorum claim; no policy replay may hide or relabel it.
- Genesis is trust-on-first-use. Every later operation is signed by an owner authorized in the immediately preceding state and binds previous/result hashes.
- Effective reader, approver, witness, quorum, access-mode, or workload changes produce explicit revisions and invalidate incompatible pending authorization.
- Principal keys are immutable. Replacement atomically carries only explicitly selected authority to a fresh same-role principal.

## Required Work

- Implement owner-signed genesis and deterministic policy revision verification.
- Implement vault-principal, approver, and witness lifecycle plus direct roles and witnessed item requirements.
- Implement normalized operations for membership, quorum, mode, operation, lifetime, workload, tombstone, and same-role replacement changes.
- Validate historical authority at each sequence and reject ambiguous forks or illegal combinations.
- Expose value-free capability and downgrade explanations without item-body decryption.

## Required Tests

Cover owner/direct role matrices, approver/witness membership and quorum matrices, zero/over-capacity quorum, duplicate/cross-role identities, mode transitions, direct-slot suppression, missing/reordered/forged operations, sole-owner protection, pending-request invalidation, replacement, rollback/fork fixtures, and property-model comparison.

## Dependencies

J03 and J05. Unblocks J07, J09, J10, J16, J20, and deferred J15.

title: J07 — Implement direct/witnessed item envelopes and rekeying
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

Implement format-v1 item protection for both direct and witnessed access after J19 acceptance. Witnessed-only items must not contain an implicit direct fallback.

## Why This Task Exists

Per-item, per-revision secrets bound the damage of any authorized release and prevent whole-vault or epoch material from becoming an ambient capability. Direct and witnessed access therefore converge only at the same narrowly scoped revision-secret boundary.

## Outcome

Each item revision has private names and values, separate descriptor/body secrets, fresh revision seals, algorithm-tagged direct and witnessed slots, signed ancestry, and atomic rekeying.

## Required Work

- Encrypt names and values independently and expose them only through authorized guarded access.
- Implement revision-scoped direct capsules and the exact J19-bound witnessed capsule construction.
- Bind lineage, item, epoch, revision, content role, suite, policy, and RevisionSealId into every context and authenticated datum.
- Never serialize, return, or reconstruct an epoch root or reusable witness contribution at the application boundary.
- Implement grant, revoke, rotate, principal replacement, witness-set change, and cover reseal as signed atomic mutations.
- Treat a usable direct slot as unilateral authority and suppress the item-level quorum claim.
- Preserve honest retention limits: neither mode can make an authorized endpoint forget a revision already opened.

## Required Tests

Cover both round trips; witnessed-only access; direct downgrade; cross-item/revision/role/seal swaps; stale policy; duplicate slots; partial/replayed contributions; retained revision-N endpoint state against revision N+1; rekey interruption; entropy failure; and absence of plaintext names, values, roots, or contributions from logs and public state.

title: J08 — Implement the mode-neutral `ItemAccessProvider`
description:

## Why This Task Exists

CLI and TUI callers must not gain a bypass merely because direct and witnessed authorization use different machinery. One narrow provider contract keeps mode, private keys, contributions, and revision secrets behind the owning boundary while giving consumers identical cleanup and failure semantics.

## Outcome

ItemAccessProvider exposes a scoped consumer operation for one authenticated descriptor/body revision, with sync core semantics and an asynchronous completion boundary suitable for witnessed requests.

## Required Work

- Validate public policy and exact slot bindings before any decapsulation or witnessed completion.
- Model direct completion plus typed witnessed pending, approved, denied, expired, stale, replay, unavailable, cancelled, and insufficient-quorum outcomes.
- Keep private identity operations inside providers.
- Pass only ProtectedRevisionSecrets to the scoped consumer and wipe intermediate direct or witnessed state on success, error, cancellation, and contained panic.
- Return stable value-free error kinds.
- Provide test doubles without production key bypasses.

## Required Tests

Cover wrong principal, role, item, epoch, policy, slot, suite, revision seal, and access mode; closure cleanup; cancellation; compile-fail raw-key/root/contribution escape; and provider failure.

title: J09 — Implement per-principal audit, checkpoints, and local receipts
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

This task covers principal-local audit and authenticated checkpoints for both access modes. J23 owns offline witness-decision receipts and server operations; both are mandatory release work.

## Why This Task Exists

A vault-wide audit key would require unrelated authority to be unlocked and would turn local verification into another shared secret. Principal-local roots and monotonic checkpoints detect tamper and rollback without putting private evidence into the portable Git artifact.

## Outcome

Each principal can verify its own append-only local audit trail and detect rollback relative to retained authenticated checkpoints without placing local custody state in the portable vault.

## Required Work

- Define signed or MACed, bounded audit entries for direct and witnessed access, request/decision state changes, and mutations.
- Link witnessed entries to bounded request, decision, receipt, policy-revision, and revision-seal identifiers without recording private names, values, manifests, contributions, or reusable authorization material.
- Store checkpoints and audit state outside .jury/vault.json under a disjoint local state root.
- Make rollback and truncation detectable relative to retained local state and report the limits for fresh clones or lost state.
- Keep paths, secrets, values, private keys, and decrypted payloads out of audit data and errors.

## Required Tests

Cover append, checkpoint, verification, truncation, reordering, substitution, rollback with and without retained state, crash boundaries, concurrent access, fresh clones, corrupted local state, and secret-leak scans.

J04, J05, and J06. Unblocks J10, J16, and J17; it also supports post-0.x J15 compatibility.

title: J10 — Deliver witnessed-aware partial-unlock sessions and scoped snapshots
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

## Why This Task Exists

Session scope is the secret-lifetime boundary visible to product surfaces. It must release only the selected descriptor or body, keep inaccessible names out of memory, and apply the same cancellation and cleanup rules whether authority is direct or witnessed.

title: J19A — Select the witnessed construction and freeze its threat model
description:
## Active Witnessed 0.x Scope

This outcome is mandatory for the experimental witnessed-access 0.x release. It remains pre-alpha, must not be used for real secrets, and may claim only properties proved under the accepted construction and deployment assumptions.

## Project Boundary

Jury is a standalone CLI/TUI plus self-hostable witness service using jury-vault format v1 and witness protocol v1. It must not depend on Jig at runtime, expose private keys, epoch roots, reusable contributions, or plaintext through adapters, or use non-generic fixtures. Direct slots remain explicitly unilateral and outside every quorum claim.

## Why This Task Exists

The endpoint-retention promise is a property of a complete construction and its
compromise model, not of “using multiple witnesses.” Selecting the construction
before schemas or provider adapters prevents availability, coordination, or a
static share-release shortcut from being mislabeled distributed authority.

## Outcome

`docs/security/witness-v1/construction.md` and
`docs/security/witness-v1/threat-model.md` select one implementable construction
and freeze its exact trust boundaries, compromise assumptions, availability and
revocation limits, direct-slot interaction, and falsifiable endpoint-retention
claim.

## Required Work

- compare maintained threshold-KEM, distributed-decryption, and other publicly
  specified candidates with applicable public analysis against the exact J01B primitive/provider evidence and J03
  domain semantics; record every rejected candidate and concrete rejection
  reason;
- specify approver, witness, endpoint, `juryd`, storage, clock, network, and
  external-anchor trust boundaries;
- state quorum, collusion, malicious-client, compromised-approver,
  compromised-witness, offline-witness, rollback, replay, expiry, restored-state,
  rotation, and recovery assumptions;
- decide whether construction-internal epoch material exists and prove that no
  conforming endpoint reconstructs or receives an epoch root or reusable
  contribution;
- define exactly what a previously authorized endpoint may retain and why that
  state can reopen only its already released revision, not a later
  `RevisionSealId` without a fresh authorized quorum;
- state direct and mixed-slot semantics: any usable direct slot is unilateral,
  defeats the item-level quorum claim, and is never an implicit fallback;
- pin the exact construction and provider-binding inputs that J19B, J19C, and J19
  must use, while retaining the pre-alpha/no-real-secrets boundary.

## Required Verification

- actor/compromise and quorum matrices cover every stated threshold and excluded
  compromise case;
- a retained-state inventory covers long-term endpoint keys, all prior requests,
  approvals, responses, contributions, revision secrets, ciphertexts, and
  plaintext;
- each claimed property maps to a construction assumption or remains an explicit
  nonclaim;
- alternative comparison uses current primary specifications and exact provider
  behavior rather than names or popularity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- one construction and provider binding are selected with no unresolved design
  alternatives;
- endpoint-retention and revision-freshness claims are explicit, falsifiable, and
  bounded by named assumptions;
- trust, compromise, revocation, rollback, replay, rotation, recovery, and

It must not depend on Jig at runtime, expose private keys, epoch roots, reusable contributions, or plaintext through adapters, or use non-generic fixtures. Direct slots remain explicitly unilateral and outside every quorum claim.

## Why This Task Exists

Individually valid signatures do not make a semantically consistent request.
The protocol must freeze one canonical meaning and one crash-safe authorization
state machine before vectors, servers, or clients can implement it differently.

## Outcome

`docs/security/witness-v1/protocol.md` and
`docs/security/witness-v1/state-machines.md` freeze canonical protocol-v1
schemas, preimages, meaningful approval rules, and deterministic request,
approval, contribution, replay, expiry, cancellation, checkpoint, anchor,
rotation, and recovery transitions for the J19A construction.

## Required Work

- define bounded canonical encodings and domain-separated preimages for requests,
  action manifests, approver descriptors and decisions, witness contributions,
  decisions, receipts, checkpoints, anchors, rotation, and recovery records;
- bind vault, genesis, item, epoch, content role, revision,
  `RevisionSealId`, policy, requester, operation, workload, expiry, nonce,
  request-specific session key, witness set, and protocol suite;
- specify `ApprovalTargetV1`, owner-signed non-secret review labels,
  entitlement-bound private-name display, field/working-directory/output-sink
  openings, label rotation, and fail-closed human approval whenever a complete
  verified meaningful representation is unavailable;
- define one common request/action-manifest validator that rejects every
  semantically inconsistent pair before display, automatic approval, approval
  signing, policy matching, or witness counting;
- define independent approver and witness membership, both quorums, duplicate
  and substitution rejection, replay, skew, not-before, expiry, cancellation,
  concurrency, key rotation, and direct-downgrade behavior;
- define first registration, strict-descendant checkpoint advancement,
  witness-behind/stale/fork outcomes, revocation propagation, restored-witness
  recovery, and the exact limit of witnessed freshness;
- define a public self-hostable external rollback-anchor interface;
- freeze database commit, signed next-candidate creation, external
  compare-and-swap, exact readback, response release, and crash reconciliation;
  only one exact signed pending candidate may reconcile, and every other
  database/anchor disagreement fails closed;
- define bounded value-free rejection codes; unknown versions, implicit direct

- every duplicated request/manifest field has an individually valid mismatch

- complete meaningful rendering and opaque-target refusal are specified at every

  recovery record;

  cross-vault/item/role/revision/seal/session, replay, expiry, quorum

description:

## Why This Task Exists

The release claim spans parsers, durable state, Git transport, cryptographic
providers, witness services, user interfaces, and child processes. Separately
authored adversarial cases and measured budgets are required because happy-path
unit tests or guessed limits cannot expose cross-boundary downgrade, rollback,
leakage, or resource-exhaustion failures.

## Outcome

Jury has separately authored negative fixtures, fuzz/property targets,
failure-injection coverage, leak scans, and recorded performance/resource
measurements across the entire security boundary.

## Required Work

- exercise format, crypto, identity, policy, item, transfer, backup,
  process, CLI, and TUI failure surfaces through executable tests;
- add coverage-guided fuzz targets for all untrusted parsers;
- add state-machine models for policy, mutations, replay, and recovery;
- inject filesystem, entropy, clock, network, database, process, and cancellation
  failures;
- model Git as an untrusted transport: whole-repository substitution, malicious
  `.git`/`.jury`, symlinked and linked worktrees, clone without local state,
  checkout/reset/force-push rollback, forged Git authorship/signatures, conflict
  markers, text merge, semantic merge partial output, and concurrent worktrees;
- prove repository-local workflows never place plaintext, identities,
  checkpoints, audit, receipts, locks, or recovery state in the Git worktree,
  index, objects, diffs, hooks, or filters;
- cover protected-memory/core-dump failure timing, device-provider conformance,
  privacy-cover history/capacity, and complete direct and witnessed end-to-end
  candidates;
- fuzz and model request/manifest consistency, approval counting, replay,
  witness checkpoint/anchor recovery, contribution assembly, receipt parsing,
  and direct-path downgrade reporting;
- run the complete corpus against at least two independent providers where the
  suite has more than one viable implementation, including cross-provider
  negative vectors and semantic-differential tests for malformed keys,
  ciphertexts, signatures, implicit rejection, canonical encoding, and limits;
- inject nonce/key reuse for every AEAD/KEM wrapper and demonstrate either the
  exact accepted misuse-resistance claim or fail-closed duplicate detection;
- exhaust every public KDF/Argon2 work, memory, lanes, length, and allocation
  limit before expensive work or allocation;
- on documented machines, measure public validation at 1/50/256 principals and
  10/100/1,000 items; policy replay at 1/100/4,096 revisions; item proofs at
  1/1,000/65,536 proofs; one-item unlock; descriptor catalogs at
  1/10/100/1,000 granted items; ten-item inject preflight; reader grant; read
  revocation/reseal at 1 KiB, 1 MiB, and near file cap; multi-item principal
  replacement; rollover at policy/proof/file caps; independent-item merge;
  transfer inspect/dry-run and Jig migration near file cap;
- measure portable/hardened identity and backup KDF wall time plus peak RSS,
  bounded rejection of hostile KDF headers, protected-memory lock/unlock/zeroize
  cost and locked-byte budget on Linux/macOS, hardware-provider cold/warm unlock
  and cancellation/concurrency behavior, every padding bucket, and proof-history
  growth under documented cover cadences;
- record no guessed absolute latency SLO; pathological superlinear behavior
  outside documented local-audit verification blocks release, and non-KDF peak
  memory stays within the 16 MiB artifact cap plus bounded touched-item state;
- scan logs, errors, JSON, receipts, snapshots, fixtures, and crash artifacts.
- challenge secret-dependent provider and wrapper paths with source-backed side-channel review plus targeted differential/statistical timing tests where measurement is meaningful; a passing timing test never replaces a constant-time contract.

- every public parser has malformed-input coverage;
- every durable transaction has before/during/after crash tests;

- provider implementations agree on accepted outputs and normalized rejection
